Prayers, fasts, and Masses are being abolished by the Reformers, yet they fail to address the abuses within these practices. Instead, Erasmus laments, they are eliminating them entirely. He questions the morals and doctrines of the Reformers, stating that there is no less indulgence for luxury, lust, or avarice among them than among those they despise. Erasmus challenges the Reformers to show him a single person who has been reformed by the Gospel from vices such as drunkenness, anger, avarice, and reviling to virtues such as sobriety, meekness, liberality, well-speaking, and modesty. Instead, he claims, many have become worse through following it.

The solemn prayers of the Church are being abolished, and Erasmus observes that there are many who never pray at all. He has not attended their conventicles, but he has seen them returning from their sermons with countenances displaying rage and ferocity, as if animated by some powerful force.

In a separate passage, Erasmus describes two islands, ten thousand furlongs distant from Africa, called the Islands of the Blest. These islands have a rich soil suitable for farming and planting, and they produce a natural fruit that is plentiful and wholesome enough to feed a leisured population. The climate is salubrious, with moderate changes in the seasons, and the winds that blow from other parts of the world dissipate before reaching the islands, bringing soft and intermittent showers or cooling breezes that gently nourish the soil. A firm belief has spread, even among the Barbarians, that these islands are the Elysian Fields and the abode of the blessed.

They enjoy moderate rains at long intervals, and winds which for the most part are soft and precipitate dews, so that the islands not only have a rich soil which is excellent for plowing and planting, but also produce a natural fruit that is plentiful and wholesome enough to feed, without toil or trouble, a leisured folk. Moreover, an air that is salubrious, owing to the climate and the moderate changes in the seasons, prevails on the islands.
